Blasted lands: scorched or irradiated by ancient war; ruins are likely.
Canyons: deep cuts left by present or vanished rivers.
Dense forest: trackless, dark, and a natural barrier.
Grasslands: broad plains or savanna forming one coherent whole.
Islands: a significant island or an archipelago off the coast.
Jagged mountains: young, tall peaks with a strong rain shadow.

Battleground: the group's land was a battlefield for stronger rivals, and they suffered for it.
Betrayal: they betrayed a trusting neighbor, or were betrayed by a false friend.
Brutal Oppression: one portion of the group was reduced to wretched servitude.
Class Struggle: classes fought openly or subtly for their own gain.
Consequences: an earlier event had long-term good or bad effects.
Decadence: old strengths crumbled into indolence and indulgence.
Depravity: vile debauchery and base habits became commonplace.
Desolation: part of their territory became uninhabitable.
Diplomatic Coup: an unusually successful alliance or affiliation was made.
Economic Boom: circumstances brought a burst of prosperity.
Enemies Within: a hostile subgroup worked evil from inside.
Evil Wizard: a malevolent sorcerer or arcane cult caused great trouble.
Exodus: a large part of the group left for a supposedly better land.
Exquisite Art: they produced art still revered today.
External War: they fought a rival nation with grave consequences.
Freakish Magic: a unique magic was developed here and its secrets kept.
Golden Age: everything went well for an extended period.
Good Wizard: a powerful magic-user protected or taught the group.
Great Awakening: a wave of reform and renewed commitment swept through.
Great Builders: they raised many vast palaces, monuments, or estates.
Great Infrastructure: they built canals, walls, roads, aqueducts, or mines.
Hero King: a ruler won legendary glory that is honored still.
Immigrants: a large group of foreigners entered more or less peacefully.
Inefficient Rule: governance was impractical, corrupt, or bound to unhelpful values.
Internal War: a civil war involved all or many of the group.
Loss of Confidence: a shock or new encounter made them doubt their own customs.
Magical Disaster: a large-scale magical calamity scarred the group.
Magical Tech: they developed a useful magical technology or infrastructure.
Natural Calamity: earthquake, drought, tsunami, or meteor strike smote them.
New Horizons: they discovered new territory, underground or elsewhere.
New Rulers: the ruling dynasty was replaced peacefully or by conquest.
Noble Function: the ruling class was expected to fill a specific role such as priest or mage.
Noble Strife: assassinations, petty wars, and mutual struggle consumed the nobility.
Plague: a vast sickness culled many and may still linger.
Poverty: circumstances reduced them to harsh simplicity for a time.
Power Brokers: they were a critical regional power broker for a time.
Praetorian Coups: soldiers or guards became the ruler's electors or deposers.
Priest King: religion and rule became deeply intertwined.
Rare Resource: a uniquely valuable resource was found or made.
Religious Fall: a once-honored religion collapsed.
Religious Rise: a powerful new religion arose.
Resource Collapse: a critical resource ran short.
Secession: a substantial part of the territory tried to leave.
Terrain Change: part of the land slowly changed its ecosystem.
Total Collapse: society fell into anarchic chaos for a time.
Twist of Fate: roll again, but reverse whether the event ultimately helped or hurt.
Urbanization: one or more cities grew vastly and spawned supporting towns.
Weak Throne: the center weakened and lords gained effective independence.
Xenophilia: they adopted foreign customs and welcomed foreigners.
Xenophobia: they turned against foreign people and cut off contact.
